subtitle: An invoice pre-filled for cleaning jobs — standard visit, deep clean, windows, carpet, move-out and supplies. Download as Excel (auto-calculating), Word, or PDF.

Pre-filled cleaning line items: standard visit, deep clean, windows, carpet, move-out, supplies
Add-ons as separate lines so recurring clients see exactly what changed
Property address field — cleaners often bill the property, not the client address

faqs.q: What should I include on a cleaning service invoice?
faqs.a: At minimum: your business name, the client and property address, a dated line-item list of services (standard visit, deep clean, add-ons), tax, and a total due. Add-ons should be itemized so recurring clients can verify what changed.

faqs.q: Is this template free to use?
faqs.a: Yes. All three formats (PDF, Word, Excel) are free to download with no email required.

faqs.q: Does the Excel version calculate tax automatically?
faqs.a: Yes. Enter your quantity and rate per line, and the subtotal, tax and total update automatically. Leave the tax rate blank if you are not required to charge sales tax.

faqs.q: Is this legal or tax advice?
faqs.a: No. Templates are for informational purposes only. Requirements vary by state — verify with your tax authority and a CPA or attorney before use.

deepDive.heading: Cleaning invoices: per-visit pricing, scope checklists and the add-ons that pay
deepDive.sub: Cleaning is priced by the visit, the hour or the square foot, and every model collapses if the scope is not written down. Here is how to invoice cleaning work so the customer knows what they paid for.

blocks.h3: Per visit, per hour or per square foot — pick one and state it
paras: Residential recurring cleaning is usually priced per visit: a standard clean for a two-bedroom apartment runs roughly $100 to $180 depending on market and frequency, with a deep clean or move-out clean at two to three times that. Hourly pricing applies to one-off and post-construction work where the scope is unknown until you arrive, typically $35 to $60 per cleaner-hour.

Commercial work is priced per square foot per visit or by the month under contract. The invoice should state which model applies, because a customer who expected per-visit pricing and receives an hourly bill will dispute the hours, and you cannot prove them wrong after the fact.
list: Recurring residential: per visit, frequency stated
Deep / move-out clean: multiple of the standard rate, listed as its own service
Post-construction: hourly with a stated minimum, or per square foot
Commercial: per square foot per visit or monthly contract value

blocks.h3: The scope checklist is the invoice's backbone
paras: The most common cleaning dispute is not quality — it is scope. The customer expected inside the oven, inside the fridge, baseboards and the inside of windows; the cleaner priced a surface clean. Attaching a short checklist to the invoice, with the areas covered and the add-ons not included, eliminates that argument permanently.

Add-ons should be priced individually and listed on the invoice when performed: inside oven, inside fridge, interior windows, blinds, laundry, garage, balcony. Each is 15 to 45 minutes of real work and none of it should be absorbed into a standard clean that was priced without it.
list: Time on site and number of cleaners, for hourly work

blocks.h3: Supplies, equipment and who provides them
paras: Whether supplies are included changes the economics by 5 to 10 percent of the job. If you supply everything, say so — it justifies the rate. If the customer supplies, state it, because a customer who runs out of product mid-clean will expect you to improvise for free.

Specialty equipment is the same story: a carpet extractor, a steam cleaner or a pressure washer for exterior work is capital equipment with a consumable cost. Price it as a line when it is used rather than burying it in a per-visit rate that assumes a mop and a vacuum.
list: Specialty equipment used and priced (extractor, steamer, pressure washer)
Consumables on recurring contracts (bags, cloths, chemicals)
Travel charge for jobs outside a stated radius

paras: Recurring cleaning is billed monthly in arrears with each visit dated, or prepaid at a discount. Either way, the invoice should record the visits performed, because that list is the evidence when a customer claims a visit was missed.

Keys, alarm codes and access are a liability question. Put the arrangement in writing on the first invoice: who holds a key, whether the alarm code is stored, and what happens if the customer is not home. The cancellation policy — typically 24 or 48 hours, with a fee below that — should appear on every invoice rather than only in the original contract.
list: Visits performed with dates, on monthly invoices
Cancellation notice period and late-cancel fee
